scope: Written prototype/callback scopes and parameter-site ownership, including typedef, decay, member, return, and composite paths.
GNU typeof expression/type-name ownership and evaluation contexts, distinct from reused runtime bounds.
Retained metadata only; this does not implement C execution or generated code.

commands.measurement_script_source:
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
root=Path('/home/dev-user/.cache/toucan/type-ownership-target/release');deps=root/'deps'
for label,source in [('alloc-changed','/tmp/toucan-checked-allocations.rs'),('corpus','/tmp/toucan-type-ownership-corpus.rs')]:
 output=f'/tmp/toucan-type-ownership-{label}'
 args=['rustc','--edition=2024','-O',source,'--extern',f'toucan_semantic={root}/libtoucan_semantic.rlib','--extern',f'toucan_target={next(deps.glob("libtoucan_target-*.rlib"))}','-L',f'dependency={deps}','-o',output]
 subprocess.run(args,check=True)
 suffix='.txt' if label=='alloc-changed' else '.log'
 with open(output+suffix,'w') as out: subprocess.run(['taskset','-c','2',output],check=True,stdout=out,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
 print(Path(output+suffix).read_text())
assert Path('/tmp/toucan-type-ownership-alloc-baseline.txt').read_bytes() == Path('/tmp/toucan-type-ownership-alloc-changed.txt').read_bytes()
commands.affinity: taskset -c 2,3 for build/test; CPU2 for the allocation/corpus binaries

checks: typeof(pointer-to-VLA update) executes at a reached declaration
typedef uses share the original bound without re-evaluating the operand
sizeof(type) distinguishes contributing array types from optional pointer type operands
alignof, generic control and scalar typeof suppress side effects
sizeof(non-VLA expression) is unevaluated; sizeof(VLA expression) evaluates its operand

default_allocations.limitation: Counts requested allocation sizes under the system allocator on three inputs, not peak RSS, runtime speed, or a universal overhead proof.

external_corpus.limitation: Compares retained versus ordinary analysis on the pinned preprocessed x86_64 Linux corpus; it is not new cross-platform C compiler differential evidence.
